transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-17
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Alvarez, Priya Nair (Redwood) — Liam O'Connor, Rhea Banerjee, Marcus Holt, Sofia Kim (TidalMesh)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
Redwood walked through integration options for a 6-week POC to validate latency/cost targets for a real-time inventory assistant. Focus on OpenAI-compatible endpoints, SDKs (Node/Python), function-calling flow for inventory updates, structured JSON output contract, and benchmarks across hosted and dedicated modes. TidalMesh asked for network/VPC considerations and SSO/KMS. Next steps: share bench plan, traces, and pricing.

[00:00:12] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intros, I'm Maya on the Redwood AE team, Diego and Priya are our SEs.
[00:00:22] Liam O'Connor: hey, Liam here, CTO at TidalMesh. quick note we have limited time zones so appreciate the fast runthrough.
[00:00:30] Rhea Banerjee: Rhea — head of data. we'll be driving the benchmarks and the eval criteria.
[00:00:36] Marcus Holt: Marcus, platform eng — i'll own logs / infra side.
[00:00:40] Maya Chen: awesome. objective for today: align on success criteria for the POC, confirm workload shape, and agree on an integration approach for SDK + function-calling, plus security needs.

[00:02:05] Diego Alvarez: quick Q to start — do you expect the assistant to call back into your systems to do inventory writes, or will Redwood host those actions?
[00:02:18] Sofia Kim: the product intent is that the assistant will return structured JSON that our backend consumes, then we do the update. so function-calling in the model would map to our internal webhook.
[00:02:33] Diego Alvarez: cool — so typical pattern: model emits structured object or uses function-calling schema, Redwood streams tokens and we can enforce an output schema. small caveat: function-calling sometimes gets mistranscribed, so we recommend schema validation + intent confidence thresholds.

[00:04:15] Rhea Banerjee: success criteria from our side — p50 end-to-end latency under 400ms for short prompts, p95 under 900ms; cost target under $X per 1M tokens (we asked for a ballpark). also accuracy on entity extraction >95% on test set.
[00:04:40] Maya Chen: that's helpful. a note: p50/p95 will vary by model variant and hosting mode. for example, a quantized 7B variant on dedicated can give sub-300ms p50 for 64-token responses but costs differ.
[00:05:02] Marcus Holt: our workload — prelim runbook: 120 average prompt tokens, average response 60 tokens, peak concurrent 220 RPS during batch windows (shipping cutover), median request size 180 tokens total. persistent KV cache hit rate estimated 30-40% for repeated tracking requests.
[00:05:30] Priya Nair: good, that KV reuse is important — Redwood's prefix/KV caching reduces cost and latency for repeated session queries. we'll include cache-aware bench scenarios.

[00:06:20] Maya Chen: Diego, can you run through SDK options briefly?
[00:06:25] Diego Alvarez: sure. we expose an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and also native SDKs. recommended pilot flow: use the OpenAI-compatible HTTP layer (so minimal code changes) and then swap to our SDK once you want streaming optimizations and connection pooling. Node + Python examples, we also have a tiny Go client if needed.
[00:06:55] Sofia Kim: we prefer minimal code changes; strong preference for OpenAI compatibility so we can reuse existing wrappers.
[00:07:02] Diego Alvarez: that's exactly the intended path. note on function-calling: OpenAI-compatible responses will include a "function_call" object; Redwood can post the function call as an internal event to your webhook, or you can consume the structured JSON payload directly.

[00:08:20] Rhea Banerjee: about structured output — we will require a strict schema for inventory_update: {sku, location_id, delta, timestamp, source_confidence}. can Redwood validate and reject malformed outputs?
[00:08:38] Priya Nair: yes — we can enforce schema at the gateway level and return a structured error. we'll also provide a JSON Schema hook so your devs can push schema revisions.

[00:09:50] Liam O'Connor: on security: we need SOC2 compliance, SAML/SSO for team access, VPC peering or private link to avoid public egress, and customer-managed KMS for any persisted embeddings. is that supported?
[00:10:10] Maya Chen: yes — for enterprise pilot we can provision Redwood Private in your VPC, or Dedicated with VPC connectivity and KMS integrations. SOC2 is in place, and we have SAML + RBAC. we'll send the security pack after the call.

[00:12:05] Marcus Holt: network question — latency to Redwood hosted region in eu-west is ~30ms from our infra. for dedicated we'd likely colocate in the same VPC / AZ. we'll need to run e2e network tests during the bench window.
[00:12:22] Diego Alvarez: recommended: we'll do a 2-hour bench window where we run hosted vs dedicated variants. bench matrix will include 3 model profiles: redwood-7b-q4 (open-compat), redwood-13b-q4f, and a smaller 3b for low-cost paths. measure p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens.

[00:14:00] Sofia Kim: do you have an examples sheet for bench metrics?
[00:14:06] Diego Alvarez: yes, Diego points to the shared bench spreadsheet (link shared in chat) — it's a simple CSV with columns: model, seq_len, concurrency, cache_on/off, batching_on/off, p50, p95, cost_estimate.

[00:15:25] Rhea Banerjee: timeline — we'd like a 6-week pilot: week 0 onboarding & infra + traces, week 1 bench runs, week 2 integration + function-calling mapping, week 3 usability QA, week 4 scale burn, week 5 acceptance. is that feasible?
[00:15:44] Maya Chen: yes, feasible. typical: 4–8 week pilots. Redwood will provide a pilot checklist and an SOW. we'll aim to start onboarding next Monday if traces come in by Friday.

[00:17:10] Marcus Holt: for bench data we can provide 48 hours of API logs and a synthetic generator for peak load (we have k6 scripts). we'll share S3 access read-only.
[00:17:22] Maya Chen: perfect. Diego — we'll need a test harness that can replay traces preserving timestamp distributions.
[00:17:28] Diego Alvarez: yup — we'll run a replay harness and synthetic variance for cold vs warm KV cache to observe cache hit benefits.

[00:18:50] Liam O'Connor: pricing — high level: how much higher is dedicated vs hosted? and is there burst capacity?
[00:19:00] Maya Chen: dedicated has a fixed monthly cost + per-token delta; hosted is pay-as-you-go. recommended for predictable traffic like yours is dedicated with burst pool for short spikes. Maya to follow up with concrete numbers in the pricing sheet.

[00:21:05] Sofia Kim: on function-calling reliability: we need deterministic outputs for inventory writes, can't have the model hallucinate an SKU and write it. what's the mitigation strategy?
[00:21:18] Priya Nair: guardrails: schema enforcement, prompt engineering templates that force constraint language, model confidence scoring, and an approval step for any low-confidence updates. also you can set the system to return only candidate suggestions which your backend post-validates.

[00:23:15] Marcus Holt: can we run an experiment where we route 10% of calls through a stronger model for critical writes and 90% through a cheaper model?
[00:23:24] Diego Alvarez: yes. Redwood routing policies support model variant routing by policy — latency-first, cost-first, or mixed. we can do canary or traffic-split during the POC.

[00:25:50] Rhea Banerjee: evaluation metrics for extraction accuracy — we'll provide a golden test set (2k examples). request: Redwood to run evals automatically and surface regressions per deploy.
[00:26:08] Maya Chen: Redwood Optimize can run the evals and trigger alerts if quality drops. we'll wire the test set into the bench harness.

[00:28:30] Sofia Kim: integration pragmatics: we want to reuse our existing OpenAI-based wrapper lib. are there header differences? token counting differences?
[00:28:45] Diego Alvarez: OpenAI-compat is minimal — same endpoints, similar request/response fields. tokenization is model-specific; we provide tooling to compute token counts and a token-meter tool in the SDK. we'll attach example changes for your wrapper.

[00:31:12] Liam O'Connor: about logs/audit: we need per-request auditing with user-id provenance and redaction for PII. how long retain logs?
[00:31:22] Priya Nair: default retention is 90 days, but for enterprise pilots we can extend or integrate with your logging sinks via syslog/Kinesis. redaction rules can be applied at ingestion if needed.

[00:33:05] Marcus Holt: embeddings — we plan a small retrieval augmentation for product descriptions; where do those vectors live? Customer-owned or Redwood-managed?
[00:33:16] Diego Alvarez: options: store in Redwood-managed vector store (encrypted-at-rest) or push embeddings to your vector DB. for regulated data you can choose customer-owned.

[00:35:40] Rhea Banerjee: any known gotchas on the OpenAI-compat route that would surprise an infra team?
[00:35:48] Diego Alvarez: two quick ones: 1) streaming semantics — we expose chunked streaming but your client lib may need small adaptions; 2) function-calling fields sometimes vary in schema shape between providers — we normalize but recommend schema enforcement client-side.

[00:37:55] Maya Chen: recap and success criteria check: bench targets (p50 < 400ms, p95 < 900ms), accuracy >95% entity extraction, cost under target (TidalMesh to confirm $ threshold), pilot start next Monday pending trace delivery.

[00:39:10] Sofia Kim: that matches. also need an SLA for the dedicated environment during the pilot.
[00:39:18] Maya Chen: yep — we'll include a pilot SLA in the SOW.

[00:41:00] Diego Alvarez: tech notes to include in the bench plan: sequence lengths used (prompt/response), concurrency ramp patterns, cache warm vs cold runs, model variants, sample payloads for function-calls, expected webhook contract and error responses. we'll share the bench CSV and a small k6 config.

[00:43:20] Marcus Holt: acceptance criteria — post-bench we'll run a 24h stability run at 50% of peak to validate memory leaks and dropped connections.
[00:43:31] Priya Nair: good call; we'll provision additional telemetry to capture connection metrics.

[00:45:45] Rhea Banerjee: any compliance docs we should see now?
[00:45:50] Maya Chen: yes — I'll send SOC2, ISO summary, data flow diagrams, and the KMS integration guide (link in follow-up).

[00:47:55] Liam O'Connor: final question — do you support post-commit hooks for function-calls? we want to trigger downstream event pipelines after a successful update.
[00:48:05] Diego Alvarez: yes — Redwood can emit events to customer webhooks or to an event bus (e.g. SNS/Kafka) on successful commits or on error states. we'll include an example.

[00:50:30] Maya Chen: ok wrapping up. next steps we'll summarize: Diego to build bench matrix and test plan; Marcus will upload traces; Maya to send pricing and pilot SOW; meet again for bench kickoff on 2026-06-25.
[00:51:05] Sofia Kim: thanks all — appreciate the clarity.
[00:51:10] Liam O'Connor: thanks — talk soon.

(occasional crosstalk, filler words, and auto-transcription artifacts present — e.g., "KV" transcribed as "K-V" or "HSM" as "H-M-S" in places).
